chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm if the Muhrim (person in Ihram) undergoes cupping, provided he does not shave or cut the hair."

This is applicable in a state of necessity, as indicated by the report we previously cited from al-Hasan al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "If one is compelled to shave the back of the head for the sake of cupping, let him shave and there is no penalty upon him."
As for doing so by choice, then that is not permissible.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.حَلْقُ الْقَفَا: Shaving the back of the head

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in Ihram to undergo cupping if it requires cutting hair?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifying the distinction between voluntary and necessary hair removal during Ihram. The text links this permissibility to the principle of *darurah* (necessity), citing a preceding narration from al-Hasan al-Sayqal to justify that if shaving the nape is required for the efficacy of cupping, it incurs no penalty, whereas voluntary shaving remains prohibited.
